summary: Frontend regression + new heat-dots test on Change Location. 14 heat dots render as expected (visual PASS). But hover produces NO tooltip and clicking a VISIBLE dot at its on-screen bounding-box center does NOT invoke the dot's click handler — instead the map-background click (handleMapPick + reverse geocode) fires. This is the exact bug the review request warned about, only now reproduced with a genuine on-screen click (not a force-click on an off-screen path).

ui_bugs.issue: Hover over a visible path.heat-dot-core does NOT show any .leaflet-tooltip element. bindTooltip appears to never activate — strongly suggests the dot's pointer events are being swallowed / another element sits above it.

Click on a visible dot at its bounding-box center fires the map's click handler (handleMapPick → photon reverse geocode) instead of the dot's own click handler. Evidence: after clicking dead-center on the Tokyo core dot (bbox 26x26 at 640,395), the single POST /api/users/location payload was {"lat":35.67514743608467,"lng":139.65270996093753,"city":"東京都, Japan"} — raw map coords + reverse-geocoded Japanese label — NOT the popular-list entry which would have persisted city='Tokyo, Japan' at exact center 35.6762/139.6503. The feed pill afterwards read '東京都' rather than 'Tokyo'. Same pattern would produce a coord-looking pill for any other city dot.

integration_issues.issue: The core.on('click', …) handler never runs. Only ONE POST was made per click (no double-fire), but it's the WRONG POST (map handler's reverse-geocode result). Likely causes to investigate: (a) another Leaflet pane / overlay above the overlayPane intercepting SVG pointer events, (b) circleMarker rendered via Canvas renderer where SVG selector still exists but pointer target differs, (c) CSS `pointer-events:none` inherited on the SVG path, (d) the halo (interactive:false) or map click handler subscribed at capture phase reading raw latlng before Leaflet dispatches to the marker.

action_items: Fix heat-dot pointer events so hover shows the tooltip AND click fires core.on('click') (persist with popular-list city name, not reverse-geocoded label). Suggested checks: force SVG renderer (map option renderer:L.svg()), add CSS `path.heat-dot-core { pointer-events: visiblePainted; cursor: pointer; }`, and verify no pane sits above overlayPane. Also consider guarding handleMapPick by inspecting e.originalEvent.target — skip when target is a path.heat-dot-core.

After fix, re-run: (1) hover shows '<City> · N people' tooltip, (2) click on Tokyo dot persists city='Tokyo, Japan' (or 'Tokyo'), pill reads 'Tokyo', not '東京都' and not a coordinate string, (3) verify GET /api/auth/me user.city matches the popular-list city string exactly.
critical_code_review_comments: ChangeLocationScreen.js L316-322: core.on('click') relies on Leaflet's own click dispatch. Adding an early-exit in handleMapPick when e.originalEvent.target?.classList?.contains('heat-dot-core') would defensively prevent the map handler from stealing the click even if Leaflet's marker dispatch fails.
ChangeLocationScreen.js heat-dot effect re-creates the entire layerGroup on every popular change; consider diffing to avoid tooltip/handler churn.

Halo circleMarker uses interactive:false which is correct, but its default fillOpacity 0.14 renders on top of the core in default Leaflet z-order because it was added first (group.addLayer(halo) then addLayer(core)) — verify the core is actually on top; if halo overlays the core, cursor/hit-test may still fall on halo despite interactive:false in some browsers.

success_rate.frontend: 50% — dots render + drag/regression pass; hover-tooltip and dot-click FAIL

context_for_next_testing_agent: Test flow that worked: 1) load app with #st= token, 2) accept cookie (button has data-testid=cookie-accept, but the emergent-badge overlay can block get_by_role click — prefer clicking the data-testid directly), 3) click [data-testid=feed-distance-badge] to open Change Location, 4) wait ~2.5s for popular fetch, 5) count path.heat-dot-core = 14. Positional trick: many dots return getBoundingClientRect w=0/h=0 (SVG path bbox quirk) — only dots INSIDE the SVG's rendered area report a real bbox. Zoom-out helps but at zoom-4 only the Tokyo dot remained on-screen for me. To reliably click a non-Tokyo dot, compute screen coords via map.latLngToContainerPoint(popular[i]) instead of relying on getBoundingClientRect. Final POST to restore Tokyo: fetch('/api/users/location', {method:'POST', headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+localStorage.n2m_token}, body: JSON.stringify({lat:35.6762,lng:139.6503,city:'Tokyo'})}) — this worked and pill returned to 'Tokyo'. Drag regression passed (0 POSTs during 200px drag).
rca of the issue: SYMPTOM: hover over a rendered path.heat-dot-core produces no .leaflet-tooltip; clicking dead-center on a visible dot bbox triggers only handleMapPick (POST body includes reverse-geocoded label like '東京都, Japan' and raw lat/lng that don't equal the popular-list center). REPRODUCTION: sign in as demo-00, open Change Location, wait for 14 dots, mouse.move(cx,cy) of any dot → no tooltip; mouse.click(cx,cy) → single POST /api/users/location with the map handler's payload, pill shows a reverse-geocoded string. MITIGATION IDEAS (for main agent): (1) ensure Leaflet uses the SVG renderer for the layer and add CSS `.heat-dot-core{pointer-events:visiblePainted;cursor:pointer}`, (2) in handleMapPick early-return if e.originalEvent?.target?.classList?.contains('heat-dot-core'), (3) verify z-order — call core.bringToFront() after adding to group, (4) if a Canvas renderer is active, circleMarker.on('click') still works but tooltip may need alwaysShow; better: switch to L.svg() explicitly. After any fix, verify GET /api/auth/me returns user.city matching popular-list city string, and pill reads that city name.
